newsitem.title: USA: US renews determination to capture war criminals.
newsitem.headline: US renews determination to capture war criminals.

text.p: The United States on Thursday underlined its determination to take indicted Bosnian war criminals into custody despite attacks on Western interests since a NATO arrest operation last week.

"If local authorities refuse to abide by their obligation to arrest indicted war criminals, we will continue to look for other ways to secure their capture," Robert Gelbard, the U.S. envoy on Bosnia, said in written testimony prepared for the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

Referring to the chief Bosnian Serb wartime leader, Gelbard said: "It is time for Radovan Karadzic to be delivered to The Hague and for the (Bosnian Serb) government to function on the basis of the rule of law, rather than as the private fiefdom of a corrupt war lord."
The United States and its allies have long insisted there can be no peace in Bosnia until indicted war criminals like Karadzic are brought to trial before the Internal Tribunal at The Hague.

Although the signers of the 1995 Dayton peace accords, including Bosnian Serb and Serbian leaders, pledged to cooperate on the war criminals issue, few suspects are in custody. NATO-led peacekeepers in Bosnia did not use their authority to arrest suspects until British troops moved last week in Prijedor to seize two suspects.
Since then, Bosnian Serbs have threatened retaliation against NATO and there have been a number of attacks, including the stabbing of a U.S. soldier.
